Rules / Correctness

SK2013 An exception is constructed and then discarded

new SomeException(...) is an expression statement, so the exception is allocated and thrown away.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since0.8
ReSharperObjectCreationAsStatement (resharper_object_creation_as_statement_highlighting)

Why

Writing new InvalidOperationException("..."); where throw new InvalidOperationException("..."); was meant is a guard clause that does nothing. The method continues on the path the author intended to abort, and the failure surfaces later somewhere unrelated. There is no legitimate reason to construct an exception as a standalone statement: an exception object that is neither thrown, returned, assigned nor passed anywhere has no observable effect beyond its own allocation. The fix is the missing keyword.

Example

Instead of:

if (count < 0) {
    new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(count));
}

Write:

if (count < 0) {
    throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(count));
}

When it does not fire

The rule fires only on an object-creation expression that is the whole of an expression statement, and only when the semantic model resolves the created type and that type derives from System.Exception. A constructed exception that is assigned, returned, passed as an argument, added to a collection or used in any other position is not an expression statement and is never seen. Construction whose constructor argument has an intentional side effect is still reported, because the exception is still discarded; that is documented rather than guarded, and no occurrence exists on either reference tree.
